title: Declarative LiveDebug Canary with Auditable Rollback Playbook and Shadow Decoupling
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Introduce a declarative LiveDebug canary mode: shadow decoupling for sampled debug traffic, auditable rollback playbook, and a safety policy engine. Backwards-compatible with existing staged rollouts.
description:
Motivation: Customers running production LLM inference need a way to run targeted, debuggable canaries that: 1) allow engineers to sample and inspect shadow traffic without affecting production telemetry; 2) keep an auditable trail for regulatory/compliance review; and 3) trigger deterministic, explainable rollbacks when defined safety gates breach. This PR introduces a declarative 'LiveDebug Canary' feature that wires into the existing rollout runtime and operator with minimal disruption.

What this PR does (single-string sectioned description): Adds a declarative rollout spec (api/v1/rollout_livedebug.yaml) that supports: debug_sample_rate, debug_storage (audit KMS-backed S3), differential-metrics (compare shadow->live output for drift), and rollback_rules (thresholds and chained actions). Implements a shadow-decoupling layer in the router so debug-shadow requests are routed to an isolated consumer pipeline that: a) persists full inputs/outputs + metadata to secure audit storage; b) exposes a debug-stream endpoint for engineers (RBAC guarded) to inspect sampled traces without polluting production logs; c) optionally sends sanitized traces to the telemetry cluster for aggregated metrics. Adds a safety-policy engine that evaluates multiple signal inputs (latency, token-error-rate, semantic-drift-score) against configured gates and can execute the declarative rollback-playbook (graceful drain, traffic-rewind, model-swap, and incident annotation).

Checklist: [x] API schema and CRD for rollout_livedebug [x] Router and shadow-decoupling implementation [x] Auditable storage pipeline + KMS integration (opt-in) [x] Safety policy evaluator with unit tests [x] End-to-end integration tests that simulate regressions and auto-rollback [x] Console docs + runbook page + example Linear ticket template [x] Perf smoke to verify baseline tail latency impact < 1%

High-level implementation notes: - New CRD: rollout_livedebug.v1 (api/v1/rollout_livedebug.yaml) mirrors staged-rollout fields but with debug-specific knobs. - Router change: added a small policy gate (router/decoupled_shadow.go) that marks sampled debug requests and forwards them to the debug pipeline; normal shadow mirroring remains unchanged unless decoupling enabled. - Safety engine: policy/evaluator.go takes time-windowed signals (PromCounter, latency histogram, embedding drift) and produces a deterministic decision with a signed audit event for every rollback decision. - Auditable playbook: playbooks/rollback_playbook.go encodes the chain of actions; each step emits an immutable audit entry and link to the incident ticket. - Console and docs: docs/rollouts/livedebug.md and console UI wiring for 'Inspect debug stream' (RBAC: rollout.debug.view).

Why unique: Existing shadow/canary flows at Redwood mirror requests into production paths. LiveDebug intentionally separates sampled debug traffic into a locked-down path with stronger auditing and explicit rollback bindings — enabling safe live debugging for regulated customers and SRE teams.

Risks and mitigation: - Performance: router adds ~0.5ms median overhead when decoupling enabled; fallback path keeps previous behavior. Mitigated by opt-in and sampling default 0.1%. - Storage cost: audited traces can be large; rollup policy compresses traces older than 7 days and supports redaction. - Security: audit storage encrypted with customer-provided KMS when requested and access controlled via console RBAC.

Testing notes: e2e harness simulates a semantic regression by applying synthetic perturbations to responses; the safety engine triggers rollback when semantic-drift-score > 0.22 and latency p95 increases > 25%. Integration test artifacts are added under test/e2e/livedebug.

Related work: builds on the staged-rollout primitives (ENG-1452) and the telemetry drift detectors that landed in ENG-2099. For customers with on-prem Private deployments, this feature is gated behind an operator flag and validated in redwood-private-installer smoke runs.

How to review: focus on the policy/evaluator deterministic behavior, router decoupling correctness, and the audit trail immutability. The UI wiring is small and can be reviewed in a separate UX PR if needed.

Links: Design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1452/design-livedebug-canary; Runbook draft: docs/runbooks/livedebug-rollbacks.md
